lines: Links drop. Wattzup tells you which one, and how to get it back.
If the server goes quiet, a banner says so: retrying every two seconds.
The numbers dim, and they're marked with the time they're from.
The status line reads Server offline, until the stream returns.
If the bike stops answering, the ride pauses: Lost the bike.
Wake it with a pedal stroke, then press Reconnect. Your ride is saved.
When it's back, a green banner says where the plan picked up, and the level it set.
Bluetooth off? Turn it on, and Wattzup connects on its own.
No bike yet? Pedal to wake it. Your ride starts as soon as it connects.
And if the bike stays off for ninety seconds, the ride ends, and your numbers are kept.
On a phone, the same words, the same button.
What the tests prove: a reconnect resumes the ride and resends the level.
And ninety seconds off ends the ride as bike shut off.
That is journey ten. Wattzup turns an Echelon bike or treadmill into a live training display.
